# ENABLE_METABOT setup

Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md` to keep that file lean. Read it only when working on this topic.

- **`ENABLE_METABOT=true/false`**: also a per-stack flag prompted for by `make new`, but **not** a shared-service flag — deliberately left out of `start.sh`'s `ENABLE_EMAIL || ENABLE_WEBHOOKS || ENABLE_SAML` checks since Metabot needs no external container, just `compose/metabot-overlay.yml` (wired into `scripts/common.sh`'s `compose()` the same way `email-overlay.yml` is). The overlay sets `MB_METABOT_ENABLED=true` plus the LLM provider/key vars (`MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER`, `MB_LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `MB_LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_BASE_URL`, `MB_LLM_OPENROUTER_API_BASE_URL`, `MB_LLM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` — all still defined in `env/common.env` as shared defaults, just no longer unconditionally passed to every stack from `compose/base.yml`). A stack with `ENABLE_METABOT=false` never references these vars at all, which is deliberate for two reasons: it avoids `docker compose`'s "variable is not set" warnings for vars a given stack was never going to use, and it keeps Metabot's Admin UI settings genuinely editable — Metabase locks a setting in the UI once it's supplied via env var, so a stack that wants to configure a different provider by hand must never receive `MB_LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the first place, not just receive it alongside `MB_METABOT_ENABLED=false`. The five LLM vars in `metabot-overlay.yml` are bare pass-through keys (`MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER:` with no value), not `${VAR:-}` — pass-through omits an unset var from the container entirely (and doesn't warn), whereas `${VAR:-}` injected an empty string. **`scripts/common.sh` must not default any `MB_LLM_*` var** — it used to `export MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER="${...:-anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6}"`, which silently re-supplied the dead Anthropic provider even with the line commented out in `env/common.env`, locking the Admin UI picker blank ("This has been set by the MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER environment variable"). To see what a running container actually received without exposing secrets, print lengths only, e.g. `docker exec <c> sh -c 'echo ${#MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER}'`. **This overlay only forwards an explicit allow-list of `MB_LLM_*` vars, not arbitrary ones** — setting a new one (e.g. `MB_LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_BASE_URL`, added here after being missing for a while) in a version env file does nothing until it's also added to this list; the container's `/api/setting` response shows `is_env_setting: false` for a var that's set on the host but not forwarded, which is the fastest way to confirm this class of miss rather than assuming the setting itself is broken. **OpenRouter model ids need the vendor prefix**: `MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER=openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, not `openrouter/claude-sonnet-4-6` (OpenRouter 400s with "not a valid model ID"; list valid ids via `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`). Validate a key with `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/key`. Leaving `MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER` unset while setting only `MB_LLM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` keeps the model selectable in the Admin UI (only env-supplied settings are locked). **The shared Anthropic key this project previously used is dead** (confirmed via a real `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` call returning `authentication_error: API key is invalid`) — OpenRouter is now the provider. Since `env/common.env` and `env/mb_versions/*.env` are gitignored and per-machine, this switch does **not** travel via git — an agent setting up a new/other machine needs to do it there directly, once the user hands over an OpenRouter key: (1) in that machine's `env/common.env`, remove or comment out `MB_LLM_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and `MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER` if it's set to an `anthropic/...` value) so no dead Anthropic key is ever forwarded; (2) add `MB_LLM_OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<the key the user gave you>`; (3) leave `MB_LLM_METABOT_PROVIDER` commented out (model becomes pickable in Admin UI) or set it to `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` per the format rule above; (4) restart any running stacks (env vars are only read at container creation); (5) validate with `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/auth/key` using that key before declaring it done.
